quote: 1. Gentlemen who prefer bonds don't know what they're missing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 2. Before you invest in any company, you should be able to give a two-minute monologue covering why you're interested in the stock, what has to happen for the company to succeed, and the pitfalls.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 3. Beware of diworseification: companies that expand into businesses they don't understand often destroy the value of the business they do.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 4. Behind every stock is a company. Find out what it's doing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 5. When stocks are attractive, you buy them. Sometimes they go down, and then you buy more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 6. If you like the product, investigate the company.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 7. Your investor's edge is not something you get from Wall Street experts. It's something you already have.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 8. You only need a few good stocks in your lifetime.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 9. I'm always on the lookout for great companies in lousy industries.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 10. A company with no debt can't go bankrupt.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 11. Sell a stock when the fundamentals of the company deteriorate, not because the price has gone up or down.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 12. When a stock you love falls and the story hasn't changed, it isn't a reason to panic; it's a reason to buy more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 13. Selling your winners and holding your losers is like cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 14. Twenty years in this business convinced me that any normal person using the customary three percent of the brain can pick stocks just as well, if not better, than the average Wall Street expert.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 15. You can't see the future through a rearview mirror.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 16. In the stock market, the most important organ is the stomach. It's not the brain.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 17. The simpler it is, the better I like it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 18. If a company's name is boring or ridiculous, and if the company does something dull or disagreeable, it's got my attention.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 19. In every industry and every region of the country, the observant amateur can find great growth companies long before the professionals have discovered them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 20. If you like the store, chances are you'll like the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 21. Even a great company can be a bad stock if you overpay for it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 22. If you spend more than 13 minutes analyzing economic and market forecasts, you've wasted 10 minutes.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 23. The real key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 24. In stocks as in romance, ease of divorce is not a sound reason for commitment.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 25. Nobody can predict interest rates, the future direction of the economy, or the stock market. Dismiss all such forecasts and concentrate on what's actually happening to the companies in which you've invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 26. Focus on the companies, not on the stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 27. The single most important thing to me in the stock market for anyone is to know what you own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 28. When you sell in desperation, you always sell cheap.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 29. Invest in what you know.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 30. Companies that buy back their own shares are among my favorites.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 31. Never invest in anything that you can't illustrate with a crayon.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 32. Insiders might sell their shares for any number of reasons, but they buy them for only one: they think the price will rise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 33. Big companies have small moves, small companies have big moves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 34. In the long run, a portfolio of well-chosen stocks and/or equity mutual funds will always outperform a portfolio of bonds or a money-market account.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 35. A stock is not a lottery ticket. It's part ownership of a business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 36. You should be able to explain why you own a stock in a way an eleven-year-old could understand.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 37. The extravagance of any corporate office is directly proportional to management's reluctance to reward the shareholders.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 38. Time is on your side when you own shares of superior companies.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 39. Nobody's smart enough to be in and out of the market successfully on a regular basis.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 40. Often, there is no correlation between the success of a company's operations and the success of its stock over a few months or even a few years. In the long term, there is a 100 percent correlation between the success of a company and the success of its stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 41. The trick is not to learn to trust your gut feelings, but rather to discipline yourself to ignore them. Stand by your stocks as long as the fundamental story of the company hasn't changed.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 42. The key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 43. The P/E ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 44. Never invest in a company without understanding what it does.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 45. Stay away from companies that are described as 'the next Microsoft'.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 46. Most investors would be better off in an index fund.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 47. Corrections are a chance to buy great companies at bargain prices.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 48. The best investors do their homework and ignore the noise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 49. Never invest in a stock based on a hot tip.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 50. Look for a niche: the best companies often dominate a small corner of the market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 51. A stock you don't understand is a stock you'll sell at the worst possible moment.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 52. Absent a lot of surprises, stocks are relatively predictable over 20 years. As to whether they're going to be higher or lower in two years, you might as well flip a coin to decide.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 53. The real money in a stock is made in the third or fourth year you own it, not in the third or fourth month.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 54. Never put money you will need within the next few years into the stock market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 55. Go for a business that any idiot can run—because sooner or later, any idiot probably is going to run it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 56. Investing is fun, exciting, and dangerous if you don't do any work.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 57. You make most of your money in a bear market, you just don't realize it at the time.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 58. Spend at least as much time researching a stock as you do choosing a refrigerator.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 59. Never invest in a company without understanding its finances. The biggest losses in stocks come from companies with poor balance sheets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 60. Getting scared out of stocks during a correction is like running out of Vermont in January because it might snow.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 61. Investing without research is like playing stud poker and never looking at the cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 62. A stock market decline is as routine as a January snowstorm in Colorado. If you're prepared, it can't hurt you.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 63. If you can't find any companies that you think are attractive, put your money in the bank until you discover some.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 64. The best stock to buy may be the one you already own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 65. I can't recall ever once having seen the name of a market timer on Forbes' annual list of the richest people in America.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 66. If you don't study any companies, you have the same success buying stocks as you do in a poker game if you bet without looking at the cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 67. Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections, or trying to anticipate corrections, than has been lost in the corrections themselves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 68. Avoid hot stocks in hot industries. Great companies in cold, non-growth industries are consistent big winners.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 69. If you aren't prepared to stomach a 50% decline in the market, you shouldn't be in stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 70. In this business if you're good, you're right six times out of ten.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 71. People who succeed in the stock market also accept periodic losses, setbacks, and unexpected occurrences. Calamitous drops do not scare them out of the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 72. The big winners more than make up for the mistakes: one tenbagger can pay for a lot of losers.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 73. Investing is more art than science.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 74. The stock doesn't know you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 75. Let your winners run.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 76. The person that turns over the most rocks wins the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 77. Earnings, earnings, earnings. I can't emphasize enough how important earnings are to the success of a stock investment.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 78. If you can't convince yourself, 'When I'm down 25%, I'm a buyer,' you shouldn't be in stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 79. Whatever method you use to pick stocks or stock mutual funds, your ultimate success or failure will depend on your ability to ignore the worry-mongers and stay fully invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 80. If you stay half-alert, you can pick the spectacular performers right from your place of business or out of the neighborhood shopping mall.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 81. The worst thing you can do is invest in companies you know nothing about.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 82. All the math you need in the stock market you get in the fourth grade.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 83. Long shots almost always miss the mark.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 84. If you invest $1,000 in a stock, all you can lose is $1,000, but you stand to gain $10,000 or even $50,000 over time.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 85. You get recessions, you have stock market declines. If you don't understand that's going to happen, then you're not ready, you won't do well in the markets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 86. If you're not willing to do the research, you have no business buying individual stocks. You'd be better off in a mutual fund.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 87. Eventually, stock prices follow earnings.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 88. Know what you own, and know why you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 89. Everyone has the brainpower to make money in stocks. Not everyone has the stomach.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 90. The best stocks to buy are often right in your own backyard.
speaker: Peter Lynch
